text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Outgoing Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said he believed the new Bulgarian president Petar Stoyanov would hand a mandate for forming a new government to the ruling Socialist Party.
-- Regional branches of the Socialist party (BSP) are likely to organise rallies in response to the street protests of the opposition, a BSP senior official said. @

-- The Socialist party leader Georgi Parvanov was elected as a chairman of the party's parliamentary group following the resignation of Krassimir Premyanov, who has attracted criticism for his business connections.

-- The situation in Bulgaria is extremely grave and extremely dangerous and whatever the solution of the political problems, it is important that the economic problems be dealt with as soon as possible, the International Monetary Fund Sofia representative Franek Roswadowski said.

-- Bulgaria's parliament should be dissolved by the end of January, Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) said. Before that an interim cabinet should be formed and it should be given a mandate to hold talks with international lending institutions, said the UDF.
-- The Sofia airport posted $100,000 loss after 169 flights were cancelled on Sunday and on Monday because of a dense fog.
-- Bulgaria's state owned Post Bank said it had posted 9.9 billion lev pre-tax profit for 1996.

-- Sofia students played a satirical interpretation of the clashes between riot police and protesters in Sofia on January 10 and January 11 as a protest against attempts by the ruling Socialist party to form a new government. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
